prerequisites.title: 10 active workspaces for Marketplace
prerequisites.detail: Install and test the app on 10 or more workspaces used in the last 28 days (sandboxes excluded) before submitting.

prerequisites.title: Public pages and test access
prerequisites.detail: You need a privacy policy, a public landing page, a public support page, and test credentials with dummy data. Slack cannot access your workspaces, so give a way to install the app yourself.

prerequisites.title: Own OAuth credentials for Composio
prerequisites.detail: Copy the client ID and secret from the Slack App Management page into a Composio auth config.

steps.title: Create Slack app and choose scopes
steps.detail: Create the app in Slack's app settings. Request the minimum scopes, using bot scopes unless you must act as a user.
steps.done_when: App exists with the scopes you need.

steps.title: Draft per-scope justifications
steps.detail: Write a reason for each scope explaining how your app uses it, and drop scopes for features not yet built.
steps.done_when: Every scope has a usage reason.

steps.title: Add Composio redirect URL
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and add it under OAuth & Permissions as an HTTPS Redirect URL.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the Slack auth config via Composio's API using your client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: Auth config returns an ID and a test connection succeeds.

steps.title: Get 10 active workspaces
steps.detail: Get real workspaces installing and using the app.

steps.title: Prepare submission materials
steps.detail: Draft the privacy policy outline, listing copy, and a demo script. The video should show install, OAuth, setup, end-to-end use and uninstall.
steps.done_when: All listing assets ready for upload.

steps.title: Record demo and submit
steps.detail: Record the video, set up test accounts and the security contact, then submit from the app's Submit to the Slack Marketplace section.

steps.title: Wait for Slack review
steps.detail: Preliminary review feedback, then functional review. Avoid resubmitting during the preliminary stage because it resets your place in the queue.

traps.detail: New installs of non-Marketplace commercial apps get 1 request per minute and 15 objects on conversations.history and conversations.replies. Custom internal apps are exempt.

traps.detail: Scopes like search:read.*, *:history, files:read and canvases:read trigger enhanced review. Admin* scopes are unlikely to be approved unless you are a partner.

traps.detail: After publishing, scope, feature or redirect URI changes need resubmission before they work. New scopes also require manually updating your OAuth URLs.

traps.detail: For a published app, install fails with unapproved_scope if the scopes are still in review or were never submitted.

traps.title: Callback domain cannot be verified by you
traps.detail: Slack requires an HTTPS redirect URL you configure, and Composio's callback domain is not one you control. To keep the Composio domain off the flow, proxy the callback through your own domain using a 302 redirect.

traps.detail: Apps without org-wide support install only on the owning workspace, and non-org-compatible scopes fail on Enterprise orgs. Org-level upgrades may need an Org Owner or Admin.

evidence.answer: The privacy policy must state what data is collected.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: How the data that is collected is used.
evidence.answer: The privacy policy must state how the collected data is used.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: How long data is kept.
evidence.answer: The privacy policy must state how long data is kept.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: How an individual can request to access, transfer, or delete their data
evidence.answer: The privacy policy must explain how an individual can request access to, transfer, or deletion of their data.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: At a minimum should be an email address or a webform.
evidence.answer: The privacy policy must give a contact method, which at minimum is an email address or a webform; a physical address alone is not sufficient.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: If your app receives data but never uses it, this must be stated in your privacy policy.
evidence.answer: If the app receives third-party data it never uses, the privacy policy must say so.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: In addition your landing page needs to be publicly accessible (i.e. not behind a login)
evidence.answer: The app's landing page must be publicly accessible, not behind a login.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: should be an actual web page created specifically for your Slack app
evidence.answer: The landing page must be an actual web page created specifically for the Slack app, not a PDF, document, or code repository link.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: There is a clear way to get in touch with your support if someone needs help, such as an email address or contact form.
evidence.answer: The app must provide a clear support channel such as an email address or contact form, without requiring an extra account.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: We expect support requests to receive a response within 2 business days
evidence.answer: Support requests are expected to receive a response within 2 business days.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Your support page needs to be publicly accessible i.e. not behind a login.
evidence.answer: The support page must be publicly accessible, not behind a login.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Make sure to keep it short and sweet at 10 words (or fewer)
evidence.answer: The listing short description should be 10 words or fewer.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Use a 1600px by 1000px size (8:5 ratio).
evidence.answer: Listing images should be 1600px by 1000px (8:5 ratio).

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Use a .jpg, .jpeg, or .png file format, and make sure the size is under 2MB.
evidence.answer: Listing images must be .jpg, .jpeg, or .png files under 2MB.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Keep your video length between 30-90 seconds.
evidence.answer: The recommended listing video should be 30-90 seconds long.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Make sure your video is publicly-accessible YouTube link, not a link to a channel or playlist.
evidence.answer: The listing video must be a publicly accessible YouTube link, not a link to a channel or playlist.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: If your Slack app integrates with another service, include the name of that service in your app name.
evidence.answer: If the app integrates with another service, the name of that service should be included in the app name.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Focus on requesting the smallest number of least permissive scopes you can while still providing a good experience.
evidence.answer: Apps should request the smallest number of least permissive scopes that still give a good experience.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: unnecessarily request a large number of scopes when there is a less permissive option.
evidence.answer: Apps that request a large number of scopes when a less permissive option exists are unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: search:read.* , *:history , files:read , and canvases:read
evidence.answer: Scopes that trigger enhanced review include search:read.*, *:history, files:read, and canvases:read.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: user token groups:write , groups:write.invites , mpim:write
evidence.answer: Scopes that trigger enhanced review include user token groups:write, groups:write.invites, and mpim:write.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: conversations.connect:write
evidence.answer: The scope conversations.connect:write triggers enhanced review.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: We are unlikely to approve broad access to workspace message/file data (e.g. user token * :history scopes) without a clear use case that requires them, such as Real-time Search or MCP server functionality
evidence.answer: Broad access to workspace message or file data needs a clear use case, such as Real-time Search or MCP server functionality, and is unlikely to be approved otherwise.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: scopes that provide extensive access to workspace data without a clear use case that requires them
evidence.answer: Scopes that give extensive workspace data access without a clear use case make an app unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: coded workflow scopes (e.g. admin.* , identity.* , search:read , workflow.steps:execute , triggers:* ).
evidence.answer: Coded workflow scopes such as admin.*, identity.*, search:read, workflow.steps:execute, and triggers:* make an app unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: use legacy/restricted scopes or methods
evidence.answer: Legacy or restricted scopes and methods make an app unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Scopes marked as required are always included; scopes marked as optional can be accepted or declined by the user without blocking installation.
evidence.answer: Required scopes are always included at install, while optional scopes can be accepted or declined without blocking installation.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: request user token *:history and files:read scopes for the collection of message and file data
evidence.answer: For automation platform apps, user token *:history and files:read scopes should not be requested for collecting message and file data.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: We will return submissions where user token scopes are being used unnecessarily.
evidence.answer: Submissions that use user token scopes unnecessarily will be returned.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: You must resubmit your app for review when you make substantial changes or updates to the features, purpose or functionality of your app.
evidence.answer: An app must be resubmitted for review after substantial changes to its features, purpose, or functionality.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Slack allows you to charge users for your app.
evidence.answer: Slack allows developers to charge users for their app.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: If you do so, you should handle payments securely and provide transparent information on your billing policy.
evidence.answer: Developers who charge for an app should handle payments securely and give transparent billing policy information.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: we require that you limit the installation of your app to Slack workspaces on our paid plans
evidence.answer: For automation platform apps, installation must be limited to Slack workspaces on paid plans.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: let users know that a paid Slack plan is required to access the AI agent in the app container
evidence.answer: For apps with the Agent or Assistant UI, customers need a paid Slack plan to access the AI agent in the app container.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your app needs Transport Layer Security (TLS) to encrypt all traffic between clients and servers.
evidence.answer: The app needs TLS to encrypt all traffic between clients and servers.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: your app must use TLS version 1.2 or greater to continue using Slack endpoints.
evidence.answer: Since February 19, 2020, the app must use TLS version 1.2 or greater to keep using Slack endpoints.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: your app must use the state parameter when requesting access to customer data during the OAuth flow
evidence.answer: The app must use the state parameter when requesting customer data during the OAuth flow, to prevent forgery attacks.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The URL you provide must HTTP 302 redirect to a fully qualified slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize URL, as per the first step of the OAuth flow
evidence.answer: For direct install, the provided URL must HTTP 302 redirect to a fully qualified slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize URL.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Select and enable Install from Slack Marketplace
evidence.answer: To enable direct install, open the app's Basic Information page, scroll to Installing Your App, and enable Install from Slack Marketplace.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: If accidentally exposed, you can regenerate it from your app settings.
evidence.answer: If the signing secret is accidentally exposed, it can be regenerated from the app settings.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: are installed on less than 10 active workspaces and have less than 10 weekly active users.
evidence.answer: Apps installed on fewer than 10 active workspaces and with fewer than 10 weekly active users are unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Active workspaces are workspaces that have been used in the past 28 days (and that are not sandboxes).
evidence.answer: Active workspaces are those used in the past 28 days, excluding sandboxes.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Note: this does not apply to security & compliance partners working with our Discovery API
evidence.answer: The installation threshold does not apply to security and compliance partners working with the Discovery API.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: By distributing your app through the Slack Marketplace, you agree to abide by the following core policies and terms:
evidence.answer: By distributing through the Marketplace, developers agree to the App Developer Policy, Slack Marketplace Agreement, Security Review, API Terms of Service, and Brand Guidelines.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: the Slack Marketplace team may use their judgment to deny any app from being listed
evidence.answer: The Marketplace team may use its judgment to deny any app from being listed, even beyond the listed criteria.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: export or backup message data.
evidence.answer: Apps that export or back up message data are unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: do not include functionality in Slack.
evidence.answer: Apps that do not include functionality in Slack are unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: only use Sign in with Slack functionality.
evidence.answer: Apps that only use Sign in with Slack functionality are unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: embed Slack into another site.
evidence.answer: Apps that embed Slack into another site are unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: replicate Slack client functionality, or are third-party Slack clients.
evidence.answer: Apps that replicate Slack client functionality or are third-party Slack clients are unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: share sensitive personal information, such as financial or health information in Slack.
evidence.answer: Apps that share sensitive personal information such as financial or health information in Slack are unsuitable.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: facilitate the sharing of third party service accounts between multiple users.
evidence.answer: Apps that facilitate sharing of third-party service accounts between multiple users are unsuitable.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: are in private beta, still being built, or have not been fully tested.
evidence.answer: Apps in private beta, still being built, or not fully tested are unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: enable financial transactions, including cryptocurrency transactions, or the minting or transfer of NFTs in Slack.
evidence.answer: Apps that enable financial transactions, including cryptocurrency, or NFT minting or transfer in Slack are unsuitable.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: use Slack data to train Large Language Models (LLMs).
evidence.answer: Apps that use Slack data to train Large Language Models are unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: perform sentiment analysis/insight generation, unless the insights/analysis provide very clear value to customers, are limited to an aggregate level, and it is clear how they are determined.
evidence.answer: Sentiment analysis apps are unsuitable unless the insights provide very clear value, are limited to an aggregate level, and show how they are determined.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: provide only an MCP server without meaningful in-Slack functionality.
evidence.answer: Apps that provide only an MCP server without meaningful in-Slack functionality are unsuitable.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: In addition, coded workflows are currently not eligible for listing in the Slack Marketplace.
evidence.answer: Coded workflows are currently not eligible for listing in the Slack Marketplace.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: If you do not own the service, make sure to not infringe on any trademarks or copyright
evidence.answer: Developers must not infringe trademarks or copyright in the app name when they do not own the service it integrates with.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: I submitted at the beginning of January and got approval in May — so the review alone took four months
evidence.answer: One developer's self-reported Marketplace review took about four months (submitted early January, approved in May).

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Slack states plainly in the confirmation email that at this stage every fix resets your place in the queue.
evidence.answer: Blocker: during initial review, any fix resets the developer's place in the queue, so polish listing copy before submitting.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: the functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions and 6 weeks for published apps resubmitting changes.
evidence.answer: Per WorkOS's reading of Slack guidance, functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions and up to 6 weeks for resubmitted published apps; preliminary review gets feedback within up to 10 business days.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: apps that do not meet this requirement will be blocked from submitting to the Marketplace
evidence.answer: Blocker: apps installed on fewer than 5 active workspaces (used in past 28 days) cannot submit to the Marketplace at all.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: we only perform a moment-in-time review and don’t conduct a code review.
evidence.answer: Slack's review checks use case, listing accuracy, functionality, TLS/request signing, and data access scope; it is not a code review, per Slack's FAQ.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: the app’s configuration (e.g. scopes, endpoints, listing data) is not updatable by a developer without them resubmitting to the Slack Marketplace team
evidence.answer: After publication, scope, endpoint or listing changes need resubmission and re-review before they take effect.
